name: Marquee
description: An endless scrolling row (or column) of content, such as logos or short quotes. It pauses on hover and focus, and can show a visible Pause button.

direction.description: Axis the content scrolls along. A vertical marquee needs a parent or className that gives it a height.

speed.description: Scroll speed in pixels per second.

gap.description: Space between items and between repeats, any CSS length.

pauseOnHover.description: Pauses while the pointer is over it or focus is inside it.

showPauseButton.description: Shows a visible Pause and Play button, so people can stop the motion (WCAG 2.2.2).

pauseLabel.description: Text of the button while moving.

playLabel.description: Text of the button while paused.

fade.description: Fades the content out at both edges.

keyboard: Tab: moves to the Pause button and to anything focusable in the items
Enter or Space: pauses or resumes when the button is focused
requirements: Moving content longer than five seconds can be paused: by the Pause button, by hover and focus-within, and by isPaused (WCAG 2.2.2)
Only the first copy of the items is in the accessibility tree; the repeats are aria-hidden and inert, so nothing is read or focused twice
The items are real DOM in the server HTML and are readable with no JavaScript
Visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion), and anything inside rdm-still, get a still row that can be scrolled by hand, with the repeats removed
In forced-colors (high contrast) mode the edge fade is removed
Scrolls the right way in right-to-left layouts
screenReader: The items are read once, in order, as ordinary content

avoid_when: Content people must read closely or act on, since moving targets are hard to use
anti_patterns: Putting essential links in a moving row without a Pause button
